images.caption: Figure 1:Left:We test the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) in robotics, using image–text features as the sensory representation and end-effector trajectories as the motor representation: a more capable embodied model should have sensory representations that align more closely with this motor representation. To validate this, we defineSensorimotor Alignment(S2\mathrm{S}^{2}).Right:We measureS2\mathrm{S}^{2}across 12 vision-language-action models (VLAs) and find thatS2\mathrm{S}^{2}correlates positively with SimplerEnv task success rate (Pearsonr=+0.717r=+0.717), providing empirical support for this PRH-inspired view of embodiment.

Figure 2:Measuring Sensorimotor Alignment (S2\mathrm{S}^{2}) by nearest-neighbor overlap.For the query episode (left), sensory neighbors (bottom right) have similar vision-text features, and motor neighbors (top right) have similar trajectories.Green checksmark shared neighbors;red crossesmark neighbors found only in the sensory set.
A larger overlap means that episodes with similar sensory representations also follow similar motor trajectories.
